decks.name: LeetCode #40 - Combination Sum II
decks.description: Find all unique combinations that sum to target where each number used at most once

cards.question: Combination Sum II: Given a collection of candidate numbers (candidates) and a target number (target), find all unique combinations in candidates where the candidate numbers sum to target. Each number in candidates may only be used once in the combination. Note: The solution set must not contain duplicate combinations.

solutions.name: Brute Force
solutions.explanation: Generate all possible subsets using backtracking, check if sum equals target, store valid combinations in set to avoid duplicates. Sort array first. At each index, include element and recurse to next index, then backtrack and exclude. Convert combinations to tuples for set storage. Finally convert set back to list of lists. Simple but uses extra space for set and generates duplicates that are filtered out. O(n*2^n) time and space.

solutions.name: Backtracking
solutions.explanation: Standard backtracking with duplicate skipping. Sort array, use binary decision tree approach. After excluding an element, skip all subsequent duplicates before recursing to avoid generating duplicate combinations. Include element at current index, recurse to next, backtrack. Then skip duplicates and exclude. Avoids set overhead by preventing duplicates during generation. O(n*2^n) time, O(n) space. More efficient than brute force.

solutions.name: Backtracking (Hash Map)
solutions.explanation: Use hash map to track element frequencies. Pre-process to get unique elements and counts. During backtracking, check if element available (count > 0), use it by decrementing count, recurse at same index to allow multiple uses until count exhausted, restore count on backtrack. Move to next unique element. Handles duplicates elegantly with frequency tracking. O(n*2^n) time, O(n) space for count map.

solutions.name: Backtracking (Optimal)
solutions.explanation: Most efficient backtracking using loop-based iteration. Sort array, use for loop from current index to iterate candidates. Skip duplicates within same recursion level (i > idx check). Break early if current candidate exceeds remaining target. Include candidate, recurse to next index (i+1 prevents reuse), backtrack. Clean duplicate handling at same level prevents duplicate combinations. O(n*2^n) time, O(n) space. Best practical performance.
